name: TDC ADMET Pgp_Broccatelli
description: Predict whether a compound inhibits the efflux transporter P-glycoprotein (1) or not (0) from its molecular structure, given as a SMILES string (endpoint Pgp_Broccatelli of the Therapeutics Data Commons ADMET benchmark group). The measured compounds are split by molecular scaffold into a training, a validation and a test part. The test part is fixed; the candidate is run five times (seeds 1 to 5), each time with a different division of the other compounds into training and validation. It receives the training and validation compounds with their values and the test compounds without, and returns one prediction per test compound. Each of the five runs is a separate process that receives only these arguments: it cannot read the evaluator's files, start other processes or open network connections, and it has 700 seconds. The score is the area under the ROC curve on the test compounds, averaged over the five runs; higher is better.
contract: fit_predict(train_smiles, train_y, valid_smiles, valid_y, test_smiles, info) -> sequence of finite numbers, one per test molecule in the given order: a score that is larger for class 1 (for example its probability). train_smiles, valid_smiles and test_smiles are lists of SMILES strings, train_y and valid_y lists of numbers; info has name, metric, kind ('regression' or 'binary') and seed. Score: mean over the seeds 1 to 5 of the area under the ROC curve on the test part, maximized.
notes: Downloaded by PyTDC at first use into data/admet
Predicts the binary P-glycoprotein inhibition label (1 = inhibitor) of 1,212 compounds from their SMILES strings, scored by AUROC.
Leaders are large tuned ensembles or foundation-model fine-tunes.
Needs PyTDC and rdkit: not in .venv-tasks, so the evaluator restarts itself under tools/venv-admet (created by the README's setup steps).

Every scoring call of the candidate runs in the main suite's sandbox (a child process with an audit hook, 700 s and 6 GB for one call): it keeps a search from coming across the test labels and is not a security boundary against a candidate written to attack the evaluator.

science_relevance.scientific_problem: Classify molecules as inhibitors or non-inhibitors of the efflux transporter P-glycoprotein (ABCB1) from their structure.
science_relevance.importance_rationale: P-glycoprotein limits intestinal absorption and brain penetration of many drugs and its inhibition causes drug-drug interactions and changes bioavailability, so inhibition is screened for early.
